conditions.text: C1. Content: an augment marked ṭ becomes the first part, one marked k the last part, of what is named in the 6th case. It places an augment (āgama) that a sūtra teaches.

quotes.quote: आदिष्टिद् भवति अन्तःकिद् भवति षष्ठीनिर्दिष्टस्य
टित्प्रदेशाः — <<आर्धधातुकस्येड् वलादेः>>[[७.२.३५]] इत्येवमादयः

conditions.text: C2. Only augments: a ṭ/k marker on a suffix or on a substitute does not bring in 1.1.46 (a suffix cannot be part of anything; इट् in the tiṅ list is a substitute of ल).

quotes.quote: टित्करणं ङीबर्थम्; न तु <<आद्यन्तौ टकितौ>> [[1.1.46]]  इत्येवमर्थम्। कुत एतत्? आद्यन्तयोरवयवत्वात्। न च प्रत्ययोऽवयवो युज्यते
इटोऽप्यादेशत्वं तेन भवतीति न भवति देशवनिध्यर्थष्टकारः

conditions.text: C3. The host: the item in the 6th case. With a 5th, the Kāśikā takes the following item (1.1.67) or, for तुक् after a long vowel, the preceding vowel.

quotes.quote: दीङ इति पञ्चमीनिर्देशादजादेर्युडागमो भवति
दीर्घात् परो यश्छकारस्तस्मिन् पूर्वस्य तस्यैव दीर्घस्य तुगागमो भवति

conditions.text: C4. A sūtra that forbids the augment (also optionally: “वा … न भवति”) places nothing, so it does not need 1.1.46. Where the absence of इट् is given as a nipātana (7.2.64) the same holds.

quotes.quote: वशादौ कृति प्रत्यये परत इडागमो न भवति
लोमसु वर्तमानस्य हृषेर्निष्ठायां वेडागमो न भवति

conditions.text: C5. सुट् (6.1.135–142) is disputed. The Kāśikā: “कात् पूर्वः” shows that सुट् is no part of anything (abhakta), and its ṭ serves 8.3.70 — so 1.1.46 is not used. The Bhāṣya (followed by the Kaumudī and the Padamañjarī): the ṭ already puts सुट् before the क of कृ, and “कात् पूर्वः” is set aside — so 1.1.46 does the work.

quotes.quote: कात् पूर्वग्रहणं सुटोऽभक्त त्वज्ञापनार्थम्
टित्करणं सुट्स्तुस्वञ्जाम् [[८.३.७०]] इत्यत्र विशेषणार्थम्

कात्पूर्व इत्यादि भाष्ये प्रत्याख्यातम्

not_licensed.why: Nyāsa raises 1.1.46 for the ṭ of इट् in the tiṅ list and rejects it: इट् is a substitute of ल like the other endings, so its ṭ is not for 1.1.46 (C2). Naming a rule in order to deny it is a ✖.

unsure.word: इट् is the augment at the start of the suffix
unsure.why: Reading इट् as “इडादिः प्रत्ययः” (a suffix beginning with इट्): Nyāsa and the Manoramā get “ādi” from the word आदि carried from 1.1.73, not from 1.1.46. Newer writers (Tattvabodhinī) say इट् is simply the beginning of the suffix — which is 1.1.46's effect — and call that anuvṛtti needless. Disputed.
